subject: English
passage: Shipwrecks are underwater archaeological sites containing the remains of vessels that have sunk over time. The Great Lakes contain hundreds of well-preserved shipwrecks from various historical periods spanning several centuries. Marine archaeologist Dr. Megan Donovan specializes in these underwater sites. At a Canadian maritime museum, she saw an old photograph of a distinctive paddlewheeler wreck and was surprised that she didn't recognize it. Donovan returned to Michigan and used sonar equipment to search a wide area of Lake Huron, scanning the lake bottom systematically. This approach suggests that Donovan thought that if she hadn't already seen it, the paddlewheeler wreck ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: must represent a type of vessel that was used before there were any shipping routes on the Great Lakes.
choices.B: is actually located in Canada, not Michigan, and isn't part of the Great Lakes shipwrecks at all.
choices.C: is probably in a section of the lake floor Donovan hadn't ever explored while diving.
choices.D: was almost certainly sunk much more recently than the other Great Lakes shipwrecks were.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of Dr. Megan Donovan and the paddlewheeler wreck. The text indicates that the Canadian maritime museum included a photograph showing a paddlewheeler wreck that Donovan hadn't known about before visiting the museum, even though Donovan 'specializes in' Great Lakes shipwrecks. Given her expertise, and her surprise at being unfamiliar with the wreck, the text strongly suggests that Donovan believed she would have noticed the wreck if she had been to its location. Thus, the text implies that the paddlewheeler wreck is likely in a section of the lake floor Donovan had not previously explored.
